newsitem.title: FINLAND: Summary of main summit conclusions.
newsitem.headline: Summary of main summit conclusions.

text.p: The following are the main conclusions from the Helsinki summit meeting between U.S. President Bill Clinton and Russian President Boris Yeltsin on Friday:
- Both agree to disagree about NATO expansion. Clinton says enlargement will go ahead at July Madrid summit, Yeltsin sticks to view that enlargement is dangerous for Moscow.

- NATO Secretary General Solana and Russian Prime Minister Yevgeny Primakov to complete talks on NATO-Russian document in the coming weeks. Document to include forum for regular consultations to allow NATO and Russia to work together.
- Both order their negotiators in Vienna to accelerate their efforts to set new limits on conventional armed forces in Europe.
- Yeltsin agreed to seek quick parliamentary ratification of START-2.

- U.S. is prepared to seek further strategic arms cuts with Russia under a START-3 after START-2 ratified. Yeltsin and Clinton agree guidelines to cap at 2,000 to 2,500 the number of strategic nuclear warheads retained by each country. START-3 reductions completed by 2007.
- Both agreed to preserve the Anti-Ballistic Missile (ABM) treaty while giving each the right to develop defences against "theatre missiles".
- Russian economy must develop to allow Russian citizens to feel benefits of democracy and free markets.
- The two agree to mobilise support to help finance billions of dollars in new investments for Russia.
- U.S. to back Russian membership of World Trade Organisation by 1998, Paris Club this year and work towards Russian membership of OECD.
- G7 nations have agreed to substantially increase Russia's role in annual meeting in June in Denver, Colorado, now to be called the Summit of the Eight.
- Yeltsin says Russia to pass a new tax administration law that clarifies authorities, responsiblities, fines and the ability to resolve disputes.
